object_description: long solitary bar with a striking exposed concrete folded roof
design_condition: the long solitaire closes the plot to the north and uses the slope to appear low on the upper side while closing the schoolyard as a three-storey public building, set back to leave the largest possible outdoor space

positive: The long solitaire closes off the plot to the north and closes the schoolyard to the south
The topography is used to keep a low volume in the upper area that refers to the settlement opposite
The volume is pragmatically set into the terrain, creating a transparent ground floor that becomes part of the surroundings
Placing the building to the southwest creates the largest possible outdoor space
The spatially striking exposed concrete folding roof creates a sense of identity
The open space develops parallel to the slope with different uses, and the new building forms its conclusion
The orientation of the uses creates an attractive staircase in front of the building
The building has a clear and well-structured programme
The ground floor is a generous, lively open space with different floor levels gathering canteen, hall, break hall and pool
A covered break area forms a smooth transition to the outdoor area and the all-weather pitch
The ground floor is topographically designed and looks like an artificial landscape
Integrating the gymnasium into the ground floor conveys an open, artificial space that also gives access to the school
The clear structural design and striking architectural expression will leave lasting memories
negative: The staircase in front of the building is somewhat in the shade
A long, inactive rear side towards the northern street allows no interaction with the surroundings
The playground areas in the gap between new and existing building are not very attractive
The position and width of the structure have a negative impact on the downdraughts despite the low height
The northern green terrace has no outdoor qualities
The two access bridges from the street are somewhat undersized
The open ground floor strategy is questioned in terms of functionality for an elementary school
The sports facilities were criticised for their functionality and the accessibility of the checkrooms is problematic
The above-average main usable area comes from oversized cluster storeys and a clearly oversized canteen
The complex folding roof construction and the large surface area burden the overall costs
The scale for an elementary school combined with the cost-intensive construction did not completely convince
